newsitem.title: USA: West Point rape court-martial goes to jury.
newsitem.headline: West Point rape court-martial goes to jury.

text.p: The court-martial of a West Point cadet accused of raping a woman classmate went to the jury on Friday after attorneys closed their cases with sharply differing interpretations of the woman's testimony.
The woman cadet had accused Cadet James Engelbrecht, 22, a senior from Conroe, Texas, of raping her at the home of another cadet in Stockholm, New Jersey, during Memorial Day weekend in May 1996.
Engelbrecht, testifying before the all-male jury of seven senior army officers on Thursday, disputed her testimony that she was raped, saying she was the aggressor in a consensual sex encounter.

The trial, which began on Tuesday, is the first of its kind since women began attending the prestigious military school in 1976, West Point authorities said. If found guilty, Engelbrecht could be sentenced to life in a military prison.
In his closing argument on Friday, prosecuting attorney Capt. Dean Raab said the 20-year-old woman had no reason to make up her story as Engelbrecht's lawyer had argued.

Witnesses testified earlier that the alleged victim was drunk on the night in question and Raab asked: "Does it make sense that someone in that condition would suddenly turn into a sexually aggressive predator in the middle of the night?"

Engelbrecht's attorney James Fitzgerald said in closing arguments that the woman had lied to investigators and kept changing her story. He said she claimed memory lapses when confronted with inconsistencies.
"The fact that she did not remember what she was doing doesn't excuse her. It was consensual," Fitzgerald said.

The woman testified she had been drinking at the time but had not consented to sex with Engelbrecht. An Army doctor confirmed the woman's testimony that she had never had sexual intercourse before the incident. He also said he had not seen any bruises on her.
She is now on leave from the military academy.
